name: PlayerUi
lead: `player.ui`: the calls `ui` has, for one player alone, plus what only one player's screen holds.

functions.name: menu
functions.signature: playerUi.menu(opts: { title: Text ?, items: { ItemSpec }, on_pick: (player: Player, n: number) -> (), on_close: ((player: Player) -> ())?, }) → Menu
functions.description: A titled grid of up to 54 items over the player's view; each pick is answered by `on_pick(player, n)`. Nothing goes in or out of it: the items are pictures, not stacks. A chest on Java, a form of buttons on Bedrock. `on_close` fires when the player puts it away without picking. A new menu replaces the open one.

functions.name: overlay
functions.signature: playerUi.overlay(opts: { corner: ("top_left" | "top_right" | "bottom_left" | "bottom_right")?, size: number ?, margin: number ? }?) → Overlay ?
functions.description: Puts a canvas in a corner of this player's screen, `size` screen pixels square at GUI scale 1 (96 by default, 16 to 511), `margin` from the edges (4 by default); nil where `player:supports("overlay")` is false.

functions.name: show
functions.description: Puts a layout on this player's screen. A client older than 1.21.4 (`player:supports("layout")`) gets a handle that shows nothing.

functions.name: dialog
functions.description: A screen of boxes, words and pictures (see "Dialogs"): a `ui.kit.window{}`, or a function that returns one and is drawn again after every click. nil where `player:supports("dialog")` is false.
